title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: scope just-in-time audit to users and groups
summary: Pass with one minor correction: the audit control path stops on the right settings page but should continue to Devices > Audit covered user activities. The changed licensing page still lists Endpoint DLP as included in the named plans. Historical correction instructions in the briefing were ignored.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Risk assessment / Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft plans user and group scoping for Endpoint DLP just-in-time auditing.
claims.quote: Enable customers to include or exclude users/user groups from Just‑In‑Time (JIT) Audit, ensuring audits are generated only for the selected users or groups.

Previously, enabling JIT automatically logged activities for users not targeted by policies.
claims.quote: Previously, when Just-in-time protection was turned on, user activities were logged automatically for users who were not targeted by policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The notice says audit logging must be explicitly configured for users or groups in audit scope.
claims.quote: With this update, audit logging must be explicitly configured so that only users or groups included in the audit scope have their activities logged.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection reaches the page holding audit and block scoping.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. 2. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Devices > Audit covered user activities'. Retain the note attributing the Devices tab and audit setting to MC1387575, which supplies those final steps.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API operation for changing JIT audit and block scoping is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview just-in-time protection settings audit scope PowerShell Set-DlpGlobalSettings Graph API Devices; "Set-PolicyConfig" "Just". Read JIT pages and Set-PolicyConfig, including EndpointDlpGlobalSettings; no documented JIT-scoping operation.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API operation for setting JIT's monitored Devices location is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview just-in-time protection settings audit scope PowerShell Set-DlpGlobalSettings Graph API Devices; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module "just-in-time" "DLP". Read JIT pages and Set-PolicyConfig; no JIT monitored-location operation.

claims.claim: The existing Devices checkbox selects a monitored location rather than selecting audited users.
claims.quote: Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: Learn supplies an Advanced hunting query to identify antimalware client versions.

claims.claim: Learn also describes using the Diagnostics page to check a device's JIT prerequisite.
claims.quote: You can also go to Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics page, and select Endpoint DLP not working card to check whether a specific device meets JIT prerequisite.
